A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CLIP-ICM research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–O are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v3 reports original CLIP-ICM experiments on DomainBed and ImageNet variants, together with ablations and domain-prompt analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and adds iWildCam evaluation results and a projection-specific ablation.

M1.justification: The interventional-data construction, projection objective in Equation (9), Algorithm 1, and prediction procedures are retained. The added projection ablation tests an existing component rather than introducing a new method.

E1.justification: Appendix J adds iWildCam-WILDS 2020, extending wildlife classification coverage to 182 animal species across additional camera-trap locations. The existing DomainBed datasets, ImageNet variants, and open-class evaluations are retained.

E2.justification: New Table 8 introduces Linear-Probe + Interventional data as a comparator against ordinary linear probing and image-based CLIP-ICM Linear-Probe. Existing benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged; the iWildCam comparison uses existing CLIP and linear-probe approaches.

E3.justification: v4 adds an iWildCam ID/OOD protocol and a matched-interventional-data control in Appendix M.5. Appendix J specifies 243 training locations, 48 test locations, and macro F1, but Table 7 says accuracy and labels ID/OOD with 48/243 locations. These reporting inconsistencies leave the exact new setting partly unclear; retained protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix M.5 adds an ablation isolating the contribution of A_inv by comparing linear probes using interventional data with and without the proposed projection. Existing augmentation, regularization, subspace-dimension, intervention-count, and domain-prompt analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Section 7 newly specifies that Tables 2–3 report means and standard deviations over five runs with different random seeds. v3 already displays uncertainty values and mentions randomized splits, but does not provide this count or interpretation. This disclosure does not establish an increase in runs.

E6.justification: New Table 7 adds iWildCam outcomes, including table-labeled OOD scores of 10.6 for CLIP and 14.1 for CLIP-ICM. Table 8 adds interventional-data-only linear-probe results averaging 74.9; its ordinary-probe and CLIP-ICM rows repeat existing results. Previously reported benchmark and ablation values are retained.

T1.justification: Appendix E adds conditional-distribution definitions and an idealized KL-matching argument leading to the probability-ratio equality in Condition 5.2. The subsequent identifiability argument and other guarantees remain unchanged. Relabeling Theorems 5.3 and 5.5 as propositions is not itself a substantive theoretical change.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about invariant causal prediction, linear identifiability, conditional OOD-risk improvement, and CLIP-ICM's empirical effectiveness. The additional experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: Appendix M.5 adds an interpretation attributing the additional generalization benefit to A_inv, supported by comparison with a probe trained on interventional data alone. Existing explanations of fine-tuning failures, hyperparameter effects, and domain-prompt limitations remain.

D1.justification: The v4 abstract adds a source-code availability statement and repository pointer absent from v3. Existing implementation documentation, GPT-4o prompts, hardware, training-time statements, and data-collection costs are retained. Repository availability was not independently verified.

R1.justification: v4 adds the WILDS reference and explicitly credits Ahuja et al. (2023) for Appendix F's proof technique. Appendix L.5 corrects its attribution to the 2021 content/style-identification work, removing the Backtracking Counterfactuals reference. Broader positioning remains stable; most other reference changes update publication metadata.

P1.justification: Edits include expanded Appendix E exposition, the new M.5 subsection, renaming Appendix J, theorem-to-proposition terminology, and updated authorship, publication, and acknowledgement text. The main narrative and section organization are largely retained.

P2.justification: v4 adds Tables 7 and 8, enlarges Table 1 and Figure 2 from single-column to full-width displays, and relocates or renumbers existing material. All six figures retain their graphical content; the overall document layout remains similar.

improvement.justification: The new projection ablation helps distinguish the method's contribution from augmentation alone, while the five-run uncertainty explanation and code-access pointer improve transparency. These provide limited, concrete benefits to an otherwise stable paper. The added iWildCam evidence broadens validation, although Table 7's conflicting metric and location labels limit its interpretability.
